title: The centrist extremist as subjectivity-class, and visibility as contested labor
description: These claims read the centrist extremist as a subjectivity-class: #470 argues it is drawn from the cognitive labor aristocracy, whose function is to translate radical energy into administration; #469 forecasts that the class is growing and holds a somatic hypothesis, and #470 specifies an embrittlement index. Companion claims from The Semantic Commodity Form (#137) and its ratification record (#765) file in advance that any visibility the archive gains is contested labor held against a standing gradient of liquidation, not a platform's grant. The page also holds unrelated claims, among them chat data tail-thinned by habituation (#856) and AI-mediated work foreclosed or absorbed by credential (#939).

claims.statement:
**Metric β — Embrittlement Index**


β(Σ) = 1 - (ΔA_Σ / ΔE)


Where ΔA_Σ is the rate of axiom revision and ΔE is the rate of encounter with counterevidence. Range 0–1. β ≈ 0: healthy — axioms revise in proportion to evidence. β ≈ 1: brittle — no revision regardless of evidence. β > 1: pathological — axioms become more rigid in response to counterevidence. This last is the centrist extremist signature: the position that hardens under precisely the pressure that should soften it.

claims.registered_title: The Pristine Fallacy: Why Chat Data Is Not a Clean Training Source
claims.statement: Chat users are, by sustained use, AI-habituated writers. A first-time user is not yet habituated, but large-scale chat corpora inevitably contain habituation in depth — the bulk of chat volume comes from repeat users whose cognitive patterns have been shaped by sustained interaction with the mediating system. Their writing — including the writing they produce as chat inputs — is shaped by this habituation. The inputs they produce are not samples from an unmediated human distribution. They are samples from a distribution that has already been tail-thinned by sustained interaction with the mediating system.
claims.falsifier: F1. If a well-powered study (N > 500, pre-registered) demonstrates that heavy AI-chat users show no statistically significant tail-thinning in their unaided writing relative to matched non-users, Ground 1 fails.
